newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open down 1.00 to 2.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open down 1.00 to 2.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents lower Tuesday in line with weakness overnight in London, traders said.
LIFFE robusta futures slumped early Tuesday, with September down $25 at the midday break at $1,605. November fell $19 to $1,611.

Monday, New York arabica futures ended lower, pressured by speculative abd trade selling of the nearby September/December switch. September fell 6.50 cents to 199.35 cents after ranging between 209.00 and 194.00 cents. December ended down 3.10 cents on the day, to 174.75 cents, while the back months closed 0.75 to 1.25 cents lower.
The September/December switch shrank to 24.60 cents compared with 28.00 cents at the close on Friday. December/March 1998 narrowed to 20.00 cents versus 22.10 cents the previous session.

On the charts, traders said September faced support at 194.00-193.00 cents, followed by 188.00 cents. On the upside, nearby resistance was seen around 201.00 cents, with the next level at 203.00 cents.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday that no damaging cold weather is expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt. Low temperatures will range from the mid-40s to mid-50s F (7-13 C).
After Monday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 327 60-kg bags as of Aug 8 to 93,792 bags. There were 35 bags of coffee was pending grading, the exchange said.
